title: variant-duel-insights-apr-2027
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the results of a focused duel-style comparison between three candidate serving variants for the 3.1 family:
- candidate-A (3.1-base-fp16): baseline onboarded variant currently in nightly shadow
- candidate-B (3.1-quant8-dyn): new quantized variant with KV cache preservation
- candidate-C (3.1-qa-calibrated): same weights as A but with post-training calibration and token-level bias fix

Goal: decide whether any candidate should be promoted to the 'staging' rung for a limited canary, or whether we should keep the current baseline until further fixes. Focus areas: end-user quality regressions (hallucination and instruction-following), latency P95 under production mix, and cost/token delta.

Quick takeaways:
- candidate-B wins on cost/token (~28% lower) and aggregate latency under batched workloads, but introduces a small (+3.2%) regression on instruction-follow rate on the internal prompt-set C (developer help).
- candidate-C shows consistent quality improvements across the creative and summarization prompt families (+4–6% normalized quality), with negligible cost delta (+2%) and small latency increase (+6% P95).
- head-to-head win-rate: C > A (57.6%), B > A (52.1%) but B loses to C (46.8%); implication: calibration (C) appears to preserve quality while quant (B) trades quality for cost.

Evaluation setup (short):
- Datasets: 6 prompt families sampled from production traces (dev-help, customer-support, summarization, translation, code-assist, casual-chat). Each family: 1.5k prompts sampled with frequency weighting matching Q1 2027 traffic.
- Metrics: composite_quality_score (0–100) = weighted mix of human-rated correctness (0–60), instruction-follow (0–20), and factuality/hallucination (0–20); latency_p95 (ms) measured on G4dn-like hardware with concurrency profile matching production shadow; cost_per_1k_tokens USD estimated from token counts and kernel runtime.
- Human eval: 900 pairwise comparisons across families (3 annotators per pair, majority vote). Annotators blinded to variant ids; instructions included explicit failure modes to flag (hallucination, omission, verbosity, unsafe).
- Automatic checks: exact-match on structured outputs (where applicable), token-length distributions, and a model text-similarity echo detector.

Win/loss summary (pairwise majority wins):
- C vs A: C wins 57.6% (wins on summarization, translation, code-assist); A wins 42.4% (wins on casual-chat small-chitchat coherence).
- B vs A: B wins 52.1% (wins on latency-sensitive prompts and short completions); A wins 47.9% (wins on instruction-following).
- C vs B: C wins 53.6% (quality-sensitive tasks); B wins 46.4% (cost/latency sensitive).

Pairwise win-rate matrix (annotator majority):
             |   A   |   B   |   C   
--------------------------------
 A (baseline) |  -    | 47.9% | 42.4%
 B (quant)    | 52.1% |  -    | 46.4%
 C (calib)    | 57.6% | 53.6% |  -   

Leaderboards (composite_quality_score, higher is better):
- candidate-C: 78.4
- candidate-A: 74.1
- candidate-B: 71.6

Operational signals:
- Latency P95 (ms): A: 240ms, B: 198ms, C: 255ms (under test rig concurrency profile)
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD est): A: $0.032, B: $0.023, C: $0.033
- Regression alerts triggered during run: B triggered 2 minor regression alerts for instruction-follow metric on dev-help family; C triggered 0 alerts; A baseline has no new alerts

Human-eval notes (qual):
- dev-help: candidate-B tended to truncate long clarifying steps, producing shorter answers that missed edge-case clarifications (annotators flagged as 'partial').
- summarization: candidate-C reduced hallucinated facts in extractive summaries (annotators noted concrete factual recall improvements).
- code-assist: candidate-C produced marginally better multi-line completions and fewer syntax errors.
- casual-chat: candidate-A retained a slightly more human tone; candidate-C sometimes produced terser replies due to calibration heuristics.

Risk and sensitivity analysis:
- Distributional sensitivity: candidate-B performs well on short-turn latency-driven workloads (search-snippets, autoreply), but suffers on long-context instruction-follow tasks. If our product mix skews to short-turn (e.g., high embedding + short generation use-cases), B could be a strong cost win.
- Calibration brittleness: candidate-C's gains rely on the post-training calibration table shipped in PR #879; we observed one prompt category (policy-related safety prompts) where calibration changed the mitigation stance — needs safety review.
- Cache behavior: quant path in B interacts with KV cache eviction heuristics; in a synthetic stress run we saw a 1.8% higher token re-computation rate, small but measurable.

Decision recommendation (proposal):
1) Promote candidate-C to a 1% traffic staging canary for 2 weeks, with the following guardrails:
   - Safety review on policy prompts (assign to security for sign-off prior to canary).
   - Monitor instruction-follow and hallucination SLOs with rolling 6-hour burndowns.
   - Disable candidate-C for any routes with strict conversational tone SLAs until we measure user-facing tone impact.

2) Keep candidate-B in experimental quant track for cost experiments but do NOT promote to staging until:
   - We address the instruction-follow truncation (engineering task: quant tokenizer/decoder adjustment, TICKET JIRA-ML-1067).
   - Re-run human eval on dev-help family post-fix to confirm improvement.

3) Maintain candidate-A as fallback baseline and continue shadow experiments for candidate-C to gather additional edge-case traces.

Rollout plan & metrics to watch during canary:
- Traffic split: 1% candidate-C, 99% baseline for 14 days. Expand only if no safety/regression alerts after 7 days.
- Metrics: composite_quality_score delta (target: non-negative), instruction-follow delta (target: >= -1%), hallucination rate (target: <= baseline + 0.5%), latency P95 (monitor but tolerate up to +10% while quality gains hold), cost impact (expected +2% but acceptable).

Open questions & next experiments:
- Should we combine quant and calibration (B+C)? Preliminary combined variant shows promise but we observed an unstable quant-kernel artifact in long context. Schedule combined-ablation once B's KV interaction is addressed.
- Expand prompt families: include transactional templates (billing/account) in next run — these were not fully covered and are higher risk for hallucination.

Appendix A: illustrative example pairs (anonymized)
- Summarization prompt: long customer email -> A produced concise summary with 2 hallucinated dates; B omitted an important clause; C produced accurate concise summary. Annotator votes: C > A > B.
- Dev-help prompt: multi-step debugging question -> B produced shorter step list and missed edge-case; majority vote favored A.

Appendix B: script and experiment artifacts
- eval script: eval/variant_duel/run_duel_3.1.sh (see linked GitHub PR)
- human eval rubric: CONFLUENCE-2345#rubric

Next steps owners:
- Asha Patel: coordinate canary rollout, gating metrics dashboard (console: route=staging/3.1-calib)
- Ben Liu: patch quant truncation (JIRA-ML-1067), run targeted dev-help re-eval
- Nora Kim: safety review on calibration effects (blocker for canary start)

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally concise; human-eval spreadsheets and raw annotator comments are in the linked Confluence page. Please comment in-thread or add reviews on the PR (#879).

Timestamped changelog:
- 2027-04-12: initial duel run completed, raw metrics ingested
- 2027-04-13: human eval majority voting completed, draft notes compiled
- 2027-04-15: added decision recommendation after sync with product and safety

(End of document)
